items.title: edie 27: Full programme revealed for flagship sustainable business event
items.summary: edie 27 is returning to London next April to drive adaptation, resilience and practical sustainable business transformation.

items.title: One week to register: How to turn climate risk insights into adaptation action
items.summary: This webinar, held in partnership with SmartResilience on 19 November, will explore why and how leading organisations are moving from simply measuring risk to actively adapting in order to protect their operations, assets and supply chains.

items.title: Shipping emissions caused almost $1trn in global economic damages, analysis finds
items.summary: New research has found that emissions from international shipping caused an estimated $963bn in global economic damages between 1990 and 2020.

items.title: Copenhagen bans fossil fuel advertising
items.summary: Copenhagen has drawn a line in the advertising sand. The municipality has voted to ban all promotion of fossil fuels and climate-harming products from its owned and controlled spaces.

items.title: FCA unveils landmark rules for ESG ratings providers
items.summary: From 2028, firms providing environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings in the UK will need authorisation from the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

items.title: COP31 jargon buster: What are the Blue Zone and Belém-Antalya Mechanism?
items.summary: With the COP31 World Leaders Summit beginning in Antalya, Türkiye, next week, this handy article defines key pieces of UN climate terminology for edie members – from the Blue Zone to the Belém-Antalya Mechanism.

items.title: Does sustainability need a bit of ‘greenmogging’?
items.summary: In my latest editor’s column, I outline why corporate sustainability needs to get comfortable trying to outshine the crowd by embracing the 2026 word of the year: ‘mogging’.

items.title: Six climate innovations ahead of COP31
items.summary: To mark the opening of COP31, edie and our innovation partner Springwise spotlight six innovations tackling some of the summit’s key priorities, from transforming plastic waste into water-capturing materials to using AI to accelerate urban greening and climate resilience.

items.title: Why treating nature loss and climate change as separate issues makes no sense
items.summary: As delegates gather for COP31 in Türkiye, Fauna & Flora's Annamaria Lehoczky argues that nature-based solutions must be central to climate action, with greater alignment between global climate and biodiversity commitments needed to unlock investment and build resilience.

items.title: Transition-ready companies outperform peers by 25 percentage points
items.summary: Companies that are more prepared for the net-zero transition have outperformed laggards over the past five years, according to the MSCI Institute.
